nodes.label: Cloudinary Media Pipeline
nodes.rationale: All uploads flow through one pipeline (multer memory -> sharp/ffmpeg -> Cloudinary -> Media table): memory buffers avoid disk writes, WebP/WebM auto-conversion standardizes media, Cloudinary offloads CDN storage, and the Media table keeps FK-linked metadata for other models.

nodes.label: convertToWebM (fluent-ffmpeg)
nodes.rationale: Uses temp files in os.tmpdir() because ffmpeg cannot stream from a Buffer; libvpx-vp9 conversion is slow, so the client should surface a processing state and a background queue is the growth path.

nodes.label: Multer Memory Storage
nodes.rationale: Buffers live in RAM; the multer limits config guards against OOM and should not be raised past ~25MB without a reason.

nodes.label: Cloudinary Streaming Upload
nodes.rationale: streamifier pipes the buffer into cloudinary.uploader.upload_stream; resource_type 'auto' is mandatory or videos are treated as images and silently truncate.

nodes.label: Media Model (Prisma)
nodes.rationale: Other models reference media by FK (e.g. Product.featuredImageId); deleting a Product does not delete Media rows or Cloudinary assets, and a Media row referenced by a Product must be disconnected before deletion.

nodes.label: Community Detection
nodes.rationale: Surfaces cross-document connections the user would not think to ask about; communities get human-written 2-5 word labels that also reshape suggested questions.

nodes.label: EXTRACTED/INFERRED/AMBIGUOUS Audit Trail
nodes.rationale: Honesty rules: never invent an edge, mark uncertainty AMBIGUOUS instead of omitting; a discrete confidence rubric replaced a continuous range because production showed models collapsing the range to a 0.5/0.85 binary.

nodes.label: Parallel Semantic Extraction Subagents
nodes.rationale: Subagents must be general-purpose (not read-only Explore) because chunk results are written to disk; dispatching all chunks in one message is the only way they run in parallel, 5-10x faster than sequential reads.

nodes.label: AST Structural Extraction
nodes.rationale: Deterministic and free; runs in parallel with semantic extraction and handles code-only updates without any LLM cost.

nodes.label: Incremental --update Re-extraction
nodes.rationale: Only re-extracts new/changed files to save tokens; prunes ghost nodes from deleted files and re-saves the manifest so the next diff runs against the current filesystem state.

nodes.label: Frontend Provider Stack
nodes.rationale: TanstackProvider > AuthProvider > SettingsProvider > ThemeProvider ordering matters: new global providers go inside ThemeProvider so theme tokens are available, unless the provider itself controls theming.

nodes.label: Pre-paint Theme Bootstrap Script
nodes.rationale: An inline script in <head> reads localStorage['dreamshop-theme-storage'] before first paint and adds the dark class to <html>; moving it to a useEffect causes a light/dark flash on every navigation.

nodes.label: Server vs Client Component Split
nodes.rationale: Default to server components; add 'use client' only for state/effects/browser APIs; never call axios from a server component because it skips Next's caching layer.

nodes.label: sendMail Utility (utils/mailer.ts)
nodes.rationale: Transporter is lazy-instantiated and cached to avoid reconnecting per call; the sendMail signature stays stable so the Gmail transporter can be swapped for Resend/SendGrid/SES if volume outgrows Gmail's 500/day limit.

nodes.label: Gmail App Password SMTP Flow
nodes.rationale: Uses App Password (not OAuth) for simplicity; requires 2FA enabled on the account, and auth failures are generic so the fix is regenerating the App Password.

nodes.label: renderOrderConfirmation Template
nodes.rationale: Template factories follow a render* pattern returning {html, text}; user input must be HTML-escaped via the escape helper in mailer.ts.

nodes.label: Non-blocking Email try/catch Pattern
nodes.rationale: Mail failures must not roll back the parent transaction - the order is already saved, so log the failure and continue; uncaught nodemailer rejections can crash the process.

nodes.label: Prisma 7 Datasource Config Split
nodes.rationale: In Prisma 7 the datasource block must declare only provider; the connection URL moves to prisma.config.ts - putting url/directUrl in the schema fails validation.

nodes.label: db push (No Migrations) Workflow
nodes.rationale: The project never had a prisma/migrations folder, so migrate dev would demand a baseline reset and try to wipe the Supabase DB; db push is the only safe sync path, and --accept-data-loss requires explicit user confirmation.

nodes.label: Dropped Commerce Models (Order/Cart/Wishlist/Coupon)
nodes.rationale: The pivot to catalog + custom orders removed checkout commerce (Order, OrderItem, Cart, Wishlist, ProductVariation, Coupon, Review and payment enums); they must not be reintroduced without checking with the user.

nodes.label: Schema-first Form Pattern (react-hook-form + Zod)
nodes.rationale: The Zod schema is the single source of truth for validation and z.infer derives the TS type, keeping client and server validating the same shape; all forms copy one shared skeleton.

nodes.label: superRefine Conditional Required Fields
nodes.rationale: Fields required only under conditions (e.g. mailingAddress only when deliveryMethod is MAILING) use superRefine so the same shape is re-validated server-side in customOrder.controller.ts.

nodes.label: Tailwind v4 @theme HSL Token System
nodes.rationale: Design tokens are HSL CSS variables declared via @theme (no tailwind.config.js) so ThemeProvider can swap the palette at runtime; hardcoded colors like bg-white break light/dark parity and are banned except opacity scrims.

nodes.label: Class-based Dark Mode
nodes.rationale: Dark mode is class-based (<html class='dark'>), set pre-paint by the layout.tsx inline script and at runtime by useThemeStore (Zustand); prefers-color-scheme media queries are banned because the user toggle takes precedence.

nodes.label: Custom-Order Quote Flow
nodes.rationale: Custom orders have no price at intake, so order amounts became nullable and a quote-request -> admin-sets-price -> payable-order conversion path replaces immediate payment; product cards swap Add to Cart for a Request a Quote link.

nodes.label: Dynamic Stripe/PayPal Config
nodes.rationale: Payment keys live in SiteSettings and are reread from the DB on every request so admin toggles take effect without a restart; secrets are stripped from public responses and only overwritten when the caller actually sends them (blank form fields preserve stored values).

nodes.label: Checkout customOrder Branching
nodes.rationale: checkout/page.tsx branches on ?customOrder=<productId>: quote flow hides cart and payment and posts to /orders/custom-request; regular flow hides disabled providers and falls back to a we-will-invoice-you panel when both are off.

nodes.label: Ginag Monorepo
nodes.rationale: The repo root is the single git repo - backend/ and frontend/ are committed and pushed together with one root .gitignore and no per-subproject .git.

nodes.label: Ginag Backend (Express 5 + Prisma 7 + Supabase)
nodes.rationale: CommonJS TypeScript backend: bcrypt+JWT auth, multer+Cloudinary+sharp uploads, socket.io realtime, fluent-ffmpeg transcoding, nodemailer via Gmail, node-cron jobs; entrypoint src/server.ts, wiring src/app.ts.

nodes.label: Ginag Frontend (Next 16 + React 19 + Tailwind v4)
nodes.rationale: State via Zustand + TanStack Query, forms with react-hook-form + zod, 3D via @react-three/fiber/drei; catalog + custom-order form with no checkout; dev port 5173.

nodes.label: Project Skills Registry
nodes.rationale: Project-level skills live under .claude/skills/ and Skills/skills.sh installs/verifies/removes them; the registry maps each skill to its trigger situation.

nodes.label: graphify Always-on Integration
nodes.rationale: Read GRAPH_REPORT.md before architecture answers, prefer graphify query/path/explain over grep for cross-module questions, and run graphify update after code changes (AST-only, no API cost).

nodes.label: Gemstone Theme API
nodes.rationale: Stores and serves global UI configurations (Sapphire, Ruby, Emerald palettes) to ensure frontend consistency.

nodes.label: Ginag Brand Identity
nodes.rationale: 64x64 rounded-square icon: an italic bold serif 'G' (Georgia) filled with an amber-to-bronze gradient (#fbbf24 to #b45309) on a near-black background (#0a0705). The luxury serif letterform and gold-on-dark palette signal a premium ecommerce brand; the 'G' matches the project name Ginag, suggesting this is the site favicon/logo mark despite the 'dreamecommerce' filename.
